newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore morning stocks weak, Van der Horst falls.
newsitem.headline: Singapore morning stocks weak, Van der Horst falls.

text.p: Singapore shares opened on a weak note on Tuesday with Van der Horst shares diving to a 45-month low of S$1.98 on poor interim results.

Dealers also said the overnight plunge on Wall Street triggered by comments from Japan's Prime Minister Ryutora Hashimoto that Japan could sell U.S. government securities had little impact on the Singapore market.

"The Dow has not really impacted on the local market for a while now," said one broker. He said all eyes was on engineering based Van Der Horst which reported a shocking 84-percent profit fall to S$4.14 million overnight.

The company also said major shareholders including Johannes Kotjo have had a portion of their shares, which were held independently by banks as collateral, sold. Van Der Horst were trading at S$2.08, down 11 cents at 0215 GMT. It topped the actives with over 8.3 million shares.
The Straits Times Industrials Index was down 3.70 points at 2,031.09. Turnover was a paltry 27 million shares.

Malaysia's MBF Capital Bhd resumed trading at sharply lower levels after Bank Negara rejected its merger proposals. It was down 57 cents at S$2.47. Informatics touche a new high of S$0.885 after a strong set of results. A Tan 65-8703083 MORE
